title: Design: a part sale row shows a dash in the labor columns
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "sbr-03-b-sbr-expanded.png" (board 4.3), "sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png" (board 4.10), "sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png" (board 4.11) and "sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png" (board 4.12) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Part sale {Part-sale-1} for {Customer-A} has Sales Representative {Sales-rep-A}, one part and no labor, and was invoiced today.
    For example: {Part-sale-1} is P-30001 with one part sold at $50.00.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open in that browser window, with the date range set to today and Show Unassigned on.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector and expand {Sales-rep-A}.
  2. Read {Part-sale-1}'s row in the Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin columns and compare it with the picture of board 4.10.
  3. Export the Expanded CSV and read the same row's Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin cells.
  4. Export the Expanded PDF and read the same cells.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Part-sale-1} shows as one row with Sales Type "Part Sales".
  • Step 2: each labor column shows a dash ("—"), as in the picture (today's report, board 4.3, shows 0.00 and $0.00 there).
  • Step 3: those cells are blank, as in the picture of board 4.11.
  • Step 4: those cells show a dash, as in the picture of board 4.12.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 10 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R9: “A part sale is one "Part Sales" row holding every dollar of the invoice.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.3 Before: expanded; 4.10 Expanded with Sales Type; 4.11 Expanded export (CSV); 4.12 Expanded export (PDF) (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: This is the design's version, held. The PRD gives the dash rule only for a work order's Labor and Parts rows (S5-R15) and for a part sale's Shop Supplies (S5-R15a); it says nothing about a part sale row's labor columns. Today's report (board 4.3) shows 0.00 / $0.00 there; the design shows a dash and blank cells (boards 4.5, 4.10 to 4.12). Waiting on the product owner: question Q-A in DESIGN-DIVERGENCE-REGISTER.json (drafted 20 Oct 2026, not sent).

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-03-b-sbr-expanded.png, sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png, sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png, sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png.

  • Design — board 4.10 title: “4.10 Expanded with Sales Type”

S1-12: Devon "Parts" ($266.18), Elliot "Labor" ($2,186.82), shop supplies ($175.50) with Labor (decision 37).” “At 1600px wide, the columns after Parts Margin scroll under the pinned Subtotal; production behaves the same.”
  • Design — board 4.11 title: “4.11 Expanded export (CSV)”

  • Design — board 4.12 title: “4.12 Expanded export (PDF)”
  • Design — board 4.12 note: “The PDF always has the Sales Type column. An empty side shows a dash. Header lines name the filters, including "Sales Type: All".”
